narrative.overview: Trove is a dark room built so that two things glow: the gold, and the art. Everything else recedes into near-black so the collection reads as treasure on a shelf and the accent reads as brass catching light. The register is product — a single owner answering 'what do I own and where can I open it' in under five seconds — so density is a virtue and controls repeat identically across catalogs. But the collector's pleasure is real and lives in the artifact: cover art is never chrome, and where a catalog is about single owned objects (Movies, Games) the posters lead.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black vault interior; depth by tonal layering, not shadow.
Gold is material, spent rarely — action and current selection only.
Cover art is treasure, lit; it never becomes decoration or chrome.
Mono numerics carry the ledger (counts, years, scores).
One sans family does all the UI work; a display face is reserved for the wordmark.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Gold appears on ≤10% of any screen. It is the only warm color in a cool field, so a single gold element commands the eye — spend it on the one action that matters and nothing else.

rules.name: The Split-Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold is action; rose is destruction. They are never interchanged and never adjacent as if equivalent. If a delete affordance is gold, it is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Color-Only-Status Rule
rules.body: Every status carries an icon and a word. Hue is redundant reinforcement, never the sole signal — the status palette collapses under red-green color vision deficiency.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: All numerics are mono and tabular-nums. A year, a count, or a score never renders in the sans; digits must align vertically down a column.

rules.name: The Wordmark Quarantine
rules.body: Unbounded appears only in the 'Trove' wordmark. It is never a UI label, a button, or a heading.

rules.name: The Tonal-Depth Rule
rules.body: Reach for a lighter surface before a shadow. Panels, toolbars, and rows separate by tone; shadow is only for elements that literally overlay the page.

dos: Do keep gold to ≤10% of any screen — action and current selection only.
Do render every number in JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums.
Do separate surfaces by tone before reaching for a shadow.
Do pair every status color with an icon and a word.
Do keep button, filter, and search vocabulary identical across Movies, TV, and Games.
Do give inputs the gold-line + gold-soft-glow focus bloom.
donts: Don't use gold and rose as if interchangeable. A gold delete button is a bug.
Don't signal status by hue alone. Never wire up .chip-dot; delete it.
Don't let cover art become chrome or decoration.
Don't put Unbounded into any UI label, button, or heading.
Don't build the streaming-service billboard, the social-film feed, or the enterprise admin panel.
Don't drop a shadow on a table row or a flat panel.
